worldcombat.skill.powertrick.summary: A sleight of hand that swaps your Attack and Defence: the flipped form holds, playing the trick again flips it back, and the window also reverts on its own.
worldcombat.skill.powertrick.use.0: Flip a high-Defence wall into an attacker for a round
worldcombat.skill.powertrick.use.1: Flip a fragile attacker into a tank for a round
worldcombat.skill.powertrick.use.2: Pick a form once the opponent's typing and play are known
worldcombat.skill.powertrick.description: Swap your Attack and Defence for %1$s s; playing the trick again reverts it, and the window reverts on its own. Pokemon use the temporary stat layer; other combatants swap attack and armour.
About %1$s pairs of two-colour cards rise and cross into each other's place; the count comes from Special Attack.
%1$s s wind-up, %2$s s recovery, %3$s s cooldown.
worldcombat.skill.powertrick.long.on: Long trick: hold window x1.9, for using the flipped form across a stretch of the fight; costs +2 wind-up and x1.3 cooldown.
worldcombat.skill.powertrick.long.off: Short trick: cheaper wind-up and cooldown (x0.85), snapping back quickly, only enough for one exchange.
worldcombat.skill.powertrick.timing: Cast on yourself; after a %2$s s wind-up it costs %4$s PP, then %3$s s recovery, %5$s s cooldown from commit.
worldcombat.skill.powertrick.growth.0: At level %1$s the hold window extends to %2$s and the cooldown from commit drops to %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.powertrick.growth.1: At level %1$s the hold window extends to %2$s and the cooldown drops again to %3$s.
On = long trick: hold window x1.9 for using the flipped form across a stretch, costing +2 wind-up and x1.3 cooldown. Off = short trick: cheaper wind-up and cooldown (x0.85), snapping back quickly. Duration trades against cast frequency.
The move is considered only when the threat is within this distance; larger means flipping into form earlier.
Below this distance the companion stops flipping and just reacts; larger means giving up the trick more often at close range.
The Attack/Defence gap (larger / smaller) must reach this to flip; raising it plays the trick only on extreme attackers or walls, avoiding pointless back-and-forth.
